hints: Complete the square on $x^2 + y^2 - 6x + 10y - 27 = 0$ to find the circle's centre $(3, -5)$ and radius $\sqrt{61}$.
Substitute $x = -2$ into the circle equation to find intersection points $P(-2, 1)$ and $Q(-2, -11)$, giving the base length of the triangle $PQ = 12$.
Find the gradients of radii $CP$ and $CQ$, determine the perpendicular tangent gradients ($m = \frac{5}{6}$ and $m = -\frac{5}{6}$), and find where the two tangent lines meet at vertex $T$.
Calculate the perpendicular height from $x = -2$ to vertex $T$ and use $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height}$.
walkthrough:
Complete the square to find the centre and radius of the circle:
$$(x - 3)^2 - 9 + (y + 5)^2 - 25 - 27 = 0 \implies (x - 3)^2 + (y + 5)^2 = 61$$
Centre is $C(3, -5)$ and radius is $R = \sqrt{61}$.

Substitute $x = -2$ to find the intersection points $P$ and $Q$:
$$(-2 - 3)^2 + (y + 5)^2 = 61 \implies 25 + (y + 5)^2 = 61 \implies (y + 5)^2 = 36$$
$$y + 5 = \pm 6 \implies y = 1 \quad\text{or}\quad y = -11$$
Thus, $P(-2, 1)$ and $Q(-2, -11)$, giving base length along $x = -2$ of $1 - (-11) = 12\text{ units}$.

Find the gradients of the tangent lines at $P$ and $Q$:
$$m_{CP} = \frac{1 - (-5)}{-2 - 3} = -\frac{6}{5} \implies m_{\text{tangent at } P} = \frac{5}{6}$$
$$m_{CQ} = \frac{-11 - (-5)}{-2 - 3} = \frac{6}{5} \implies m_{\text{tangent at } Q} = -\frac{5}{6}$$

Write the equations of the tangents and find their intersection vertex $T$:
$$\text{Tangent at } P: \quad y - 1 = \frac{5}{6}(x + 2) \implies y = \frac{5}{6}x + \frac{8}{3}$$
By symmetry about $y = -5$:
$$-5 = \frac{5}{6}x + \frac{8}{3} \implies \frac{5}{6}x = -\frac{23}{3} \implies x_T = -\frac{46}{5} = -9.2$$

Calculate the perpendicular height and area of the triangle:
$$\text{Height} = |-2 - (-9.2)| = 7.2 = \frac{36}{5}$$
$$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} \times 12 \times \frac{36}{5} = 6 \times \frac{36}{5} = \frac{216}{5} = 43.2$$
